source.title: Scaling Model-Generated Distillation Data Can Make Latent Teacher Traits More Recoverable
source.authors: Zhichen Dong; Zhi-Xuan Liu; Yuanjiu Fan,; Xiangtian Li; Shu-Yang Zhang; Chao Yang

page_placements.theme: Multiple traits in one teacher interfere

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Uses a filtered off-task teacher-to-student distillation setup and behavioral readouts to test trait transfer, and varies the number of independent carrier examples. The scale sweep extends the subliminal-learning protocol discussed in the paper.
record.gate_note: Rows cover reported behavioral transfer, cross-model transfer, scale/adaptation robustness, and experiments bearing on the proposed signal mechanism. The paper also cites results from other work; cited findings are not recorded as rows. Detailed dual-trait pair-level examples and DoRA/OPD results are not included below; they are noted in rows_left_out.
record.test_reason: Reproduces the original recipe: a system-prompted Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct teacher, filtered number-only carrier data, a LoRA-SFT student and a one-word preference readout. It adds matched no-trait references and varies carrier scale, LoRA rank, adaptation method, carrier type, teacher perturbation (GSM8K-SFT, evil system prompt) and teacher/student family. Its own results bear on versions A, B, C, D and E.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct, with two additions. The authors' central claim is that more independent off-task carrier data makes induced teacher traits more recoverable and more target-specific, shifting them from coarse attractors toward the intended trait. They also call the update-space probes diagnostic rather than mechanistic, and say cross-model mismatch attenuates transfer but is not a safeguard.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the filtered, semantically off-task teacher-generated carrier and student fine-tuning/readout structure associated with subliminal learning, but focuses on data scale, matched no-trait references, scale-dependent localization, and several extensions rather than simply reproducing the original study. Uses LoRA SFT by default, with additional adaptation variants.
record.method_sensitivity: Transfer varies with number of independent carrier examples, carrier composition, prompt order in dual-trait conditions, model-family match, and LoRA rank. Higher LoRA rank attenuates number-carrier transfer; richer carriers support larger adaptation spaces.

fits_no_version.finding: Dual-trait teachers: traits compete under a shared carrier. The first-mentioned trait dominates, and mixing prompt orders balances joint recovery.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Multiple hidden traits in one carrier interact and compete rather than transfer additively.

record.problems: The authors describe the work as controlled probes rather than full industrial distillation reproductions. Closed-set localization applies only to preference traits; behavioral readouts may miss effects outside selected prompts or scoring rules. Some reported values are figure-only. Update-space probes are diagnostic and do not establish the full encoding mechanism. Cross-model preference effects are noisier and weaker than same-model effects.
record.rows_left_out: Detailed DoRA results (Table 4), OPD and rank-ablation results beyond the LoRA ranks recorded here (Table 5), GSM8K-reasoning and Alpaca-carrier preference-transfer aggregates (Table 6), and dual-trait pair-level results (Figures 6 and 8) are omitted to keep the record focused on the principal claim versions. Cross-model preference figure results are summarized in r6; other figure-level model-family comparisons are not separately extracted.

untested.parts: Evaluation prompts different from those in training are not compared. One fixed 60-prompt readout family is used throughout. Full-parameter SFT is not run on the number-only carrier.
Not tested: no prompt-only insertion of tokens.
Token entanglement and a gradient-based argument are not tested.
The BeaverTails harmful-response teacher and the XSTest forced-choice results are described but not reported with values.

missing.what: DoRA rank-16 ablation: all four animal targets become top-ranked by 40K (e.g. bear +10.70 Δgap).
On-policy distillation (reverse KL): −0.15/−0.35 at 10K, +1.30/+1.66 at 40K, +2.15/+2.30 at 80K.
Non-number carriers: GSM8K reasoning traces (Δgap +2.45 to +2.58, math accuracy within 1pp of control) and Alpaca instruction data (+2.38 to +3.27).
Same-model scope runs on Llama3.1-8B, Qwen3-4B, Vicuna-7B and Gemma-3-4B.
Further cross-model pairs Qwen2.5-7B→Qwen2.5-3B and Llama→Qwen, described as showing similar scale trends.
HEx-PHI refusal-prefix probability essentially unchanged under the evil teacher; XSTest and BeaverTails harmful-response teacher diagnostics.
Intermediate evil-teacher rates: LLM 10.7% / 23.0%, human 11.7% / 25.3% at 10K / 20K.

record.verdict_notes: This is not an original source, so verdicts are given. The Table 7 and Table 9 trajectory values differ for the same conditions. Several key results are figure-only or text-only (r1, r2, r5–r9, r41). The authors caution that the GSM8K readouts may reflect answer-format residuals rather than clean reasoning transfer. The default student is Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, so the 'not stated' subjects in r32–r51 are presumably that model.

versions.untested_parts: The paper tests preference traits, task competence, and safety posture through restricted off-task carriers, including number-only data, reasoning traces, and instruction data. It does not test every possible trait or carrier.
Tests cross-model preference transfer and identity transfer, but does not establish a general rule for all teacher/student model pairings.

Tests an evil-system-prompt safety posture and reports unsafe-response rates. It does not test every harmful or alignment-relevant trait; the harmful-response teacher extension is described without its result values in the provided text.

Tests masking of the first teacher–base divergence token and probes local update-space effects. Does not test token entanglement or a gradient-based mechanism; the authors state that the geometry probes do not explain the full mechanism.
Tests LoRA ranks and reports a full-parameter SFT result with a richer carrier. It does not compare alternative evaluation-prompt sets or report whether the result changes across such sets.
No prompt-only insertion of linked tokens without fine-tuning is tested.

relationships.reason: Target lift and localization rise with scale (r1–r4). The effect holds at fixed total steps (r5). Δgap reaches about +10 / +8 at 80K (r32–r37). Math readouts rise versus flatter controls (r7–r9).
relationships.display_finding: Target lift and localization grew with carrier scale, also at fixed total steps, and Δgap reached about +10 and +8 at 80K. Maths readouts from the GSM8K-SFT teacher also rose relative to flatter controls.
